reports.title: Indice des Prix à la Consommation (IPC)
reports.publisher: Institut National de la Statistique de Djibouti (INSTAD)
reports.description: Djibouti's national CPI. INSTAD's institutional identity and existence are confirmed via its own founding decree (Décret n°2021-236/PR/MEFI, "Les statuts de l'Institut de la Statistique de Djibouti (INSTAD)... sont approuvés"), and the IMF's 2025 Article IV report (Country Report No. 25/276) reproduces CPI/inflation figures for Djibouti in its tables. HOWEVER: INSTAD's own live CPI pages (instad.dj/ipc.php) are JavaScript-rendered and returned no extractable text this round — base year, publication frequency, and any COICOP/IMF-Manual methodology citation could NOT be independently confirmed from INSTAD's own document this round. Secondary aggregators (TradingEconomics/FRED, mirroring World Bank data) suggest a "2005=100" rebasing, but this is a World Bank figure, not an INSTAD primary-document statement, so it is excluded per the branch's evidence standard. Flagged for a future session with rendering-capable browser access.
reports.cadence_note: Frequency not independently confirmed this round; the agency and its CPI mandate are confirmed, but the bulletin's own cadence statement was inaccessible.

reports.title: Stratégie Nationale de Développement de la Statistique — Schéma Directeur de la Statistique 2011-2015
reports.description: Djibouti's national statistics development strategy (2011-2015 — an older document; a newer edition may exist and was not searched for this round). Names AFRISTAT directly: "La création de l'Observatoire économique et statistique d'Afrique subsaharienne (AFRISTAT), plus d'une décennie auparavant, en a été le premier signe" [The creation of AFRISTAT, more than a decade earlier, was the first sign of this]. Separately names COMESA in connection with trade-statistics harmonisation (not CPI specifically): "le Marché commun des pays de l'Afrique de l'Est et de l'Afrique australe (COMESA) avec l'harmonisation des statistiques du commerce extérieur" [COMESA, with the harmonisation of foreign trade statistics]. Also references the African Charter on Statistics's development by the AU Commission. Djibouti's own INSTAD-founding decree separately confirms accession to AFRISTAT via "Loi n°176/AN/12/6ème L" — note this law number implies a 2012 legislature session, a discrepancy against this corpus's earlier af-grok-synthesis.json history note citing a 2010 AFRISTAT accession year for Djibouti; flagged, not resolved.
reports.cadence_note: One-off foundational strategy document (2011-2015 planning horizon, likely superseded by a newer edition not located this round).

dependencies.basis: Djibouti's own national statistics strategy names AFRISTAT's founding as a formative event for the national statistical system: "La création de l'Observatoire économique et statistique d'Afrique subsaharienne (AFRISTAT), plus d'une décennie auparavant, en a été le premier signe." General institutional acknowledgment rather than a CPI-methodology-specific citation, so 'cites' rather than 'methodology_depends_on', matching the Guinea/Madagascar convention for support-mention-only findings. `afristat-ihpc-guide-2014` already exists in the corpus — reused per the branch's node-id discipline.

Djibouti's strategy document names COMESA specifically in connection with foreign-trade-statistics harmonisation: "le Marché commun des pays de l'Afrique de l'Est et de l'Afrique australe (COMESA) avec l'harmonisation des statistiques du commerce extérieur." NOTE: this is about trade statistics, not CPI/inflation specifically — recorded as 'cites' with the domain caveat made explicit here rather than assigned an inflation-specific relationship. `comesa-treaty-establishing` was minted this same round (af-sudan.json) and is reused here for the second time.

A French technical-committee document ("Comité technique Foncier et développement," not a Djiboutian government document) quotes Loi n°174/AN/02/4ème L (7 July 2002) Articles 80 and 93 on fiscal transfers to territorial collectivities ("Des dotations et transferts de l'État"; "Une dotation globale de l'État est consentie pour le fonctionnement") with specific article numbers — a real, quotable citation, but from a secondary/third-party source rather than Djibouti's own Journal Officiel text (not locatable this round). Consistent with this branch's standing practice of not minting secondary-sourced legal paraphrase as a report node (matching the earlier UNICEF Angola and NAYMOTE Liberia precedents) — recorded here as a strong lead for a future session with better access to the Journal Officiel de Djibouti.
